title: Mixed quotient compatibility of the whole-system coefficient comparison
statement: Fix the model family of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-models] and the finite evaluation law of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-finite-laws]. The mixed law inherits that same finite evaluation datum and supplies section-identity quotient restriction coordinates of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-transitions]. For every coefficient inclusion $E\le F$, $m\le n$, and normalized input $M$, require the actual source/target whole-system transition square of $b(M)$ to commute. Require the actual quotient/inclusion ring square, with the quotient maps of [def-sp-coefficient-tower-shriek-interfaces], to commute, and require both transition words of [def-sp-field-shriek-system-transition-words] to equal their common finite word: the specified finite comparison for $R_n\to S_m$, followed by compact support of scalar extension of the actual input-system transition. The first word evaluates $b$ at $n$ then reduces the target system; the second reduces the source compact-support system then evaluates $b$ at $m$. All reductions are derivedTransition transposes, and all coordinate maps are those of the inherited EvaluationLaw. This defines a predicate, without asserting it holds; it is not merely a finite coefficient cocycle.
